Examples

  • verba nunc generāliter accipī volō, nam duplex eōrum intellēctus est; alter, quī omnia per quae sermō nectitur significat …; alter, in quō est ūna pars ōrātiōnis, legō, scrībō

    I take ‘words’ here in the general sense, for the word has two meanings: one covers everything of which speech is woven, the other one part of speech, like legō, scrībō (I read, I write)Quint. 1.5.2

    In the entry for verb

  • jam satis est. … verbum nōn amplius addam

    That’s enough now. … I won’t add another word.Hor. S. 1.1.120–121
